none: Introductory attribution and transmission chains only; no reading content.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Qālūn and al-Bazzī the first of two matching open hamzas is treated specially; the first of a kasra pair is softened, while the first of a damma pair is read between-between before the second is fully articulated.
rows.anchor: قالون، والبزي، وسهلا الأولى من المكسورتين، ومن المضمومتين بين بين مع تحقيق الثانية

rows.speaker: الجمهور من المغاربة وسائر العراقيين
rows.claim: Most Maghribi and Iraqi transmitters for Qālūn and al-Bazzī replace the first hamza in بالسوء إلا with wāw and assimilate the preceding wāw; Ibn al-Jazarī calls this the selected transmission and sound by analogy.
rows.anchor: فأبدل الهمزة الأولى منهما واوا وأدغم الواو التي قبلها فيها الجمهور من المغاربة وسائر العراقيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Dānī says no other facilitation is permissible, but Ibn al-Jazarī objects that his rule applies only when wāw is extra; here it is a root consonant, so the original facilitation is naql.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي لا يجوز في التسهيل غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makki calls dropping the vowel the best form and says it was not transmitted from Qālūn; Ibn al-Jazarī says he read it from Qālūn and al-Bazzī, judging it strong by analogy but weak in transmission.
rows.anchor: قد قرأت به عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some performance authorities and Makki also give between-between for the first hamza; al-Shāṭibiyya includes it as a second option, al-ʿUnwān omits it, and Ibn Bulayma reports both forms.
rows.anchor: وسهل الهمزة الأولى منهما بين بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against a reported between-between option for the hamza in النبيء, Ibn al-Jazarī prefers the majority's assimilation, which he considers correct in both analogy and transmission.
rows.anchor: والصحيح قياسا ورواية ما عليه الجمهور من الأئمة قاطبة

rows.speaker: سبط الخياط
rows.claim: Sibt al-Khayyāṭ uniquely reports Qālūn dropping the first of two damma hamzas through Ibn Būyān, contrary to other transmitters.
rows.anchor: وقد انفرد سبط الخياط في كفايته عن الفرضي

rows.speaker: ابن مهران
rows.claim: Ibn Mihrān uniquely reports Qālūn dropping the first hamza in all three matching-vowel categories, contrary to other transmitters.
rows.anchor: وانفرد ابن مهران، عن ابن بويان بإسقاط الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In some rasm forms, وقرآنا فرقناه and قرآنا عربيا is abbreviated with the letters qāf-rā-nūn; other alifs are omitted for lightness.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حذف في بعضها من وقرآنا فرقناه في سبحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When multiple similar hamzas meet, the hamza image is omitted to avoid writing two shapes; the rule also covers damma hamza before wāw and kasra hamza before yāʾ.
rows.anchor: فلم يكتب للهمز في ذلك صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of hamza in several forms of أولياء is absent in most Iraqi codices but present in other codices; some codices also omit it in إن أولياؤه, while the alif before hamza in البينة is unanimously omitted.
rows.anchor: فكتب في أكثر مصاحف أهل العراق محذوف الصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza's image was omitted where alif deletion brought two written forms together; the raised form was analogized to the lowered form, and إن أولياؤه aligned with وما كانوا أولياءه.
rows.anchor: وإنما حذفت صورة الهمز من ذلك

rows.speaker: الغازي بن قيس، ونافع
rows.claim: The hamza image in the three occurrences of جزاؤه in Joseph is reported deleted by al-Ghāzī b. Qays and transmitted by al-Dānī from Nāfiʿ, due to old-script similarity between wāw and zāy.
rows.anchor: فحكى حذف صورة الهمزة فيها الغازي بن قيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All codices write تراء with one alif, but scholars disagree whether the retained alif is the first or second; al-Dānī's view is introduced.
rows.anchor: فلما تراء الجمعان في الشعراء بألف واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī says al-Yazīdī's unqualified fatḥ of الناس would not prove that form or invalidate contrary transmission; al-Yazīdī's book indicates his fatḥ was a personal choice.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك على أن الفتح اختيار منه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن داود الحربي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarbī reports from Abū ʿAmr that imāla of الناس in the genitive is a Hijazi dialect and that Abū ʿAmr used it; al-Hudhali also transmits it through al-Dūrī and others.
rows.anchor: ذكر عبد الله بن داود الحربي عن أبي عمرو أن الإمالة في الناس في موضع الخفض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most transmitters and regional reader communities report fatḥ for Abū ʿAmr; only two Yazīdī routes explicitly transmit imāla, but Ibn al-Jazarī accepts both from al-Dūrī and has read both.
rows.anchor: والوجهان صحيحان عندنا من رواية الدوري عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza via Khalaf inclines ضعافا; reports differ for Khallād, with some transmitting imāla and others both forms. Makki and many Iraqi readers prefer fatḥ, while Ibn al-Jazarī accepts both as read.
rows.anchor: وأما ضعافا فأماله حمزة من رواية خلف

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الشذائي، وأبو الحسن بن المنادي، وابن حبش
rows.claim: One group opens words such as الناس when stopping with sukūn, reasoning that the kasra causing imāla has disappeared; they also report this approach from Basran readers and particular routes from Warsh and Hamza.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب أبي بكر الشذائي وأبي الحسن بن المنادي وابن حبش

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority preserve full imāla or the between-between form at pause, since pause is incidental and the word's original connecting form was imāla; this is the dominant teaching and practice.
rows.anchor: وذهب الجمهور إلى أن الوقف على ذلك في مذهب من أمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī says both stop forms are sound from al-Sūsī and that he read both; he limits the fatḥ-only report to particular routes, while the prevalent practice sustains imāla.
rows.anchor: وكلا الوجهين صحيحان عن السوسي نصا وأداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author analogically gives preference to imāla in this phrase for those who otherwise take fatḥ, because assimilation leaves a kasra after the alif.
rows.anchor: وقد تترجح الإمالة عند من يأخذ بالفتح من قوله في النار لخزنة جهنم

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads فأزلهما with an alif after zāy and an ungeminated lām; the other readers omit the alif and geminate the lām.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة فأزلهما بألف بعد الزاي وتخفيف اللام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads Adam in the accusative and kalimāt in the nominative; the others read Adam nominative and kalimāt accusative.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير بنصب آدم ورفع كلمات

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads لا خوف عليهم with fatḥ on fāʾ and no tanwīn; the other readers use nominative with tanwīn.
rows.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب لا خوف عليهم حيث وقعت بفتح الفاء

words: فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر، وابن كثير، والبصريان
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathīr, and the two Basrans read لا رفث and لا فسوق with nominative and tanwīn; Abū Jaʿfar does the same for لا جدال, while the specified remaining readers use fatḥ without tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير، والبصريان فلا رفث،

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، والبصريان
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the Basrans read the listed لا بيع, لا خلة, لا شفاعة, لا خلال, لا لغو, and لا تأثيم forms with nominative and tanwīn; the text also says the remaining readers read the seven words with nominative and tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وكذا قرأ ابن كثير، والبصريان (ولا بيع،

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر، وحمزة، والكسائي، وخلف
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Hamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read the rāʾ of غير الله in the genitive; the others read it in the nominative.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف بخفض الراء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads with ḍamma on tāʾ, kasra on hāʾ, and nafs in the accusative; the others use fatḥ on both initial consonants and nominative nafs.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بضم التاء وكسر الهاء، ونصب السين

rows.speaker: روح
rows.claim: Rawḥ reads ولا ينقص with fatḥ on yāʾ and ḍamma on qāf; Ruways varies by route, while the other transmitted routes and remaining readers use ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥ on qāf.
rows.anchor: فروى روح بفتح الياء وضم القاف

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: One route in al-Mubihj from Rawḥ uniquely has والذين يدعون in the third person, matching the reading attributed to al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة الحسن البصري

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads كذلك يجزي with yāʾ, ḍamma, fatḥ on zāy, and nominative كل; the others read with nūn, fatḥ, kasra on zāy, and accusative كل.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو بالياء وضمها وفتح الزاي

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو، وحمزة، وخلف، وحفص
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Hamza, Khalaf, and Ḥafṣ read بينات منه without alif as singular; the other readers use the alif plural form.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة وخلف وحفص بغير ألف

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza makes the hamza of السيئ quiescent in connected recitation to ease consecutive vowels; al-Fārisī cites Arabic usage, and Ibn al-Jazarī validates the reading, also reporting it from al-Aʿmash, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة بإسكان الهمزة في الوصل لتوالي الحركات تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At pause Hamza substitutes a pure yāʾ for the hamza; Hishām does likewise when lightening by the Ḥalwānī route, while Hamza additionally has between-between at pause.
rows.anchor: وإذا وقف حمزة أبدلها ياء خالصة، وكذلك هشام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Reports differ on Ibn Kathīr's takbīr range: some start it at the end of al-Ḍuḥā through the end of the Qurʾān, while Qunbul's cited report starts at the beginning of al-Inshirāḥ; the author finds no authority saying it begins at the start of al-Ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: يكبر من خاتمة " والضحى " إلى آخر القرآن فإذا قرأ

rows.speaker: أبو العلاء الهمداني، وصاحب التجريد
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ gives al-Sūsī one takbīr route from the opening of al-Inshirāḥ to the end of al-Nās; al-Tajrīd reports it via Ibn Ḥabash, and Ibn al-Jazarī read it through that route.
rows.anchor: قطع له بالتكبير من فاتحة ألم نشرح إلى خاتمة الناس وجها واحدا

rows.speaker: سائر الرواة عن السوسي
rows.claim: Other transmitters from al-Sūsī report no takbīr, like the general body of readers; some authorities had instead adopted takbīr for all readers or at every sūra opening.
rows.anchor: وروى سائر الرواة عنه ترك التكبير كالجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī discusses takbīr in prayer because leading qirāʾāt authorities treated the question and transmitted reports from early reciters and jurists, matters relevant to reciters and others.
rows.anchor: وأما حكمه في الصلاة وإن كان أكثر القراء لم يتعرضوا لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers agree on a quiescent sīn in the Tur phrase كسفا because it is described by the singular masculine ساقطا.
rows.anchor: وإن يروا كسفا لوصفه بالواحد المذكر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير، وابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read قال سبحان as a statement with alif, matching Meccan and Syrian codices; the others read the imperative قل without alif, matching their codices.
rows.anchor: وابن عامر (قال) بالألف على الخبر

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads لقد علمت with ḍamma on tāʾ; the other readers use fatḥ.
rows.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي بضم التاء، وقرأ الباقون

rows.speaker: المدنيان، وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: In ربي إذا, the two Medinan readers and Abū ʿAmr open the yāʾ of the first-person possessive form.
rows.anchor: وفيها من ياءات الإضافة واحدة) ربي إذا فتحها المدنيان، وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: المدنيان، وأبو عمرو، وابن كثير، ويعقوب
rows.claim: For لئن أخرتن, the two Medinans and Abū ʿAmr retain the extra yāʾ in connection, while Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb retain it both connected and paused.
rows.anchor: لئن أخرتن أثبتها وصلا المدنيان، وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: المدنيان، وأبو عمرو، ويعقوب، ورويس عن قنبل
rows.claim: For فهو المهتد, the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr retain the extra yāʾ in connection; Yaʿqūb and Ruways from Qunbul by Ibn Shanabūdh retain it both connected and paused.
rows.anchor: فهو المهتد أثبتها وصلا المدنيان، وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says to call on God while certain of an answer and with an attentive heart; al-Tirmidhī transmits it, and al-Ḥākim calls its chain sound.
rows.anchor: لحديث أبي هريرة يرفعه " ادعوا الله وأنتم موقنون بالإجابة.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Another report from Abū Hurayra says to make one's request great, since nothing is too great for God; it is recorded by Muslim, Ibn Ḥibbān, and Abū ʿAwāna.
rows.anchor: وعنه يرفعه أيضا " إذا دعا أحدكم فليعظم الرغبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report raised from Ibn ʿAbbās recommends supplicating with the palms and wiping the face afterward; it is narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Ḥākim in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: لحديث ابن عباس يرفعه " إذا سألتم الله فسلوه ببطون أكفكم،

rows.speaker: السائب بن يزيد عن أبيه
rows.claim: Al-Sāʾib b. Yazīd reports from his father that the Prophet raised his hands in supplication and wiped his face; Abū Dāwūd records it.
rows.anchor: وعن السائب بن يزيد عن أبيه - رضي الله عنهما - أن النبي

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar reports that the Prophet did not lower raised hands after supplication until wiping his face; al-Ḥākim records it in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and al-Tirmidhī calls it sound in some copies.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه قال:

rows.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām rejected wiping the face after supplication in his fatwas; Ibn al-Jazarī says he likely had not encountered these hadiths.
rows.anchor: ورأيت بعض علمائنا، وهو ابن عبد السلام في فتاواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī recounts seeing the Prophet in a vision during a crisis in 792 AH; he asked for supplication for himself and the Muslims, and the Prophet prayed and wiped his face.
rows.anchor: أنا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في شدة نزلت بي وبالمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Qurʾān completion, although some reciters chose fixed personal prayers, Ibn al-Jazarī recommends staying with the Prophet's transmitted supplications because his comprehensive words suffice and provide the model.
rows.anchor: واختيارنا أن لا يجاوز ما ورد عنه

rows.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وخلف، وحفص، ويعقوب
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Ḥafṣ read both ميت and الميت with gemination; Yaʿqūb joins them for الميت, while the remaining readers lighten the form.
rows.anchor: ووافقهما أيضا حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص في ميت والميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers geminate the form for someone who has not yet died, as in وما هو بميت, because death has not yet become an accomplished state; other contexts differ.
rows.anchor: على تشديد ما لم يمت نحو وما هو بميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For adjacent sukūns where the next word begins with a ḍamma hamza, readers vary the preceding consonant's vowel across nūn, dāl, tāʾ, tanwīn, lām, and wāw: ʿĀṣim and Hamza generally use kasra, Yaʿqūb excepts wāw, Abū ʿAmr excepts lām, and others use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: كسر النون وضمها من (فمن اضطر، وأن احكم،

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان
rows.claim: Reports for Ibn Dhakwān vary on tanwīn: some routes give kasra throughout; many authorities except these two phrases with ḍamma, while al-Ṣūrī transmits ḍamma throughout. Ibn al-Jazarī accepts both route forms.
rows.anchor: واختلف عن ابن ذكوان، وقنبل في التنوين

rows.speaker: قنبل من طريق ابن شنبوذ
rows.claim: The correct Ibn Shanabūdh route for Qunbul uses kasra on tanwīn when the preceding word is genitive, as in خبيثة اجتثت and منيب ادخلوها, and ḍamma elsewhere; other reports give ḍamma throughout.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن شنبوذ عن قنبل كسر التنوين إذا كان عن جر

rows.speaker: الداني، وطاهر بن غلبون، وابن شريح
rows.claim: Al-Dānī, Ṭāhir b. Ghalbūn, and Ibn Shurayḥ report that Hamza and al-Kisāʾī stop on أيّا before ما; Ibn Ghalbūn also notes a Ruways disagreement, while the others stop on ما.
rows.anchor: أبي عمرو الداني في التيسير، وشيخه طاهر بن غلبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most authorities give no specific stop ruling; because أيّا and ما are separate words in the rasm, Ibn al-Jazarī finds both stop points permissible and closest to the governing principles.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الأقرب إلى الصواب، وهو الأولى بالأصول

rows.speaker: ابن سعدان
rows.claim: Ibn Saʿdān reports that Hamza and Salīm stop on أيّا, but he considers stopping on ما better because ما is an augmenting particle attached to أيّ.
rows.anchor: ابن سعدان والوقف الجيد على (ما)
